title: Lock Codes With a Given Digit Sum

concept.title: Stop a branch as soon as the sum can no longer be reached
body: A code has `n` digits, each from 0 to 9 (leading zeros are allowed), and the digits must add up to `s`. Build the code digit by digit. After some digits, the amount `remaining` is what the other digits still have to give. If `left` digits are still to be chosen, they can give anything from `0` to `9 * left`.

The check `rest > 9 * (left - 1)` is a **bound**: even if all later digits were 9, the sum could not be reached, so the branch is not entered. With such bounds every branch that is started leads to at least one answer, so there is no wasted work. Increasing digits are tried first, so the codes come out in increasing order.

statement: A code has `n` digits (0 to 9, leading zeros allowed). Print all codes whose digits add up to `s`, in increasing order, one per line. If there is no such code, print `-1`.
outputFormat: The codes in increasing order, one per line, or `-1`.
hints: Choose the digits from left to right, smaller digits first.
Pass the sum that is still missing as an argument.
Skip a digit if the rest would be negative or larger than 9 times the number of digits left.

starter.python:
n, s = map(int, input().split())

# Your code here

explanation: Digits are chosen from left to right. A digit is skipped when the remaining sum would be negative or more than the later digits can supply, so every started branch ends in a valid code; smaller digits first give increasing order.
solution.complexity: Time O(number of codes * n), at most about 6000 codes.

code.python:
def build(n, remaining, current, out):
    left = n - len(current)
    if left == 0:
        if remaining == 0:
            out.append("".join(current))
        return
    for d in range(10):
        rest = remaining - d
        if rest < 0 or rest > 9 * (left - 1):
            continue
        current.append(str(d))
        build(n, rest, current, out)
        current.pop()

n, s = map(int, input().split())

out = []
build(n, s, [], out)
print("\n".join(out) if out else -1)
